location_qualifier: Taivu Point, about twenty-two miles east of Lunga Point
source_locator: R2225: ch. IV, citing 17th Army Operations, I; R2228: C25080232800 pp. 21–23 (stamps 0459–0461), first echelon of 916 men left Truk at 05:00 on 16 August on six destroyers, landed near Taivu Point in the middle of the night of 18 August, assembly complete at 23:00; R2226: Appendix A lists the Ichiki Unit
notes: Miller, chapter IV, citing 17th Army Operations, I: the first echelon, about 1,000 men including Colonel Ichiki, landed at Taivu Point about 18 August 1942. Zimmerman, Appendix A, lists the Ichiki Unit. Confidence 0.7 (Miller reporting the Japanese 17th Army record, with the Marine official history listing the unit). The 17th Army operations record images now read (C25080232800, stamps 0459–0461) give the first echelon as 916 men, departing Truk at 05:00 on 16 August and completing assembly at Taivu at 23:00 on the 18th. Confidence remains 0.7.

location_qualifier: sand bar at the mouth of the Ilu River (battle often called Tenaru)
source_locator: R2225: ch. IV; R2226: the Ilu / Tenaru narrative; R2228: C25080232800 pp. 23–24 (stamps 0461–0462), the lead reached the east bank of the 中川 (Ilu / Tenaru) on the night of 20 August, and the first echelon was destroyed on the afternoon of 21 August under a counterattack with six tanks
current_activity: assaulting the eastern perimeter at the Ilu
notes: Miller, chapter IV, and Zimmerman: about 0310 on 21 August 1942 the first echelon of the Ichiki Force tried to cross the Ilu sand bar and was destroyed. The unit is recorded as destroyed on this date. Confidence 0.7 (Army and Marine official histories). The 17th Army operations record images now read (C25080232800, stamps 0461–0462) place the fight on the east bank of the 中川 and date the tank counterattack to the afternoon of 21 August. Confidence remains 0.7 (already supported by Miller and Zimmerman).
